stages.spec:
# Mobile home page polish — single stage

## Why this will be good
The mobile home page currently feels chunky and unfocused: an oversized valuation strip that gets clipped, a horizontally-scrolling services strip with full-bleed images that buries the message, a generic 'Handpicked Properties' label with no transaction-type framing, and tall Communities cards that read as a column of stripes. Fixing all six surfaces in one cohesive pass — tighter rhythm, icon-first density, segmented tabs for buy vs rent, richer Communities affordance — makes the mobile home page feel like a product, not a stack of marketing blocks. Benchmark feel: Airbnb mobile home (dense, scannable, every section earns its real estate). Production-ready: works at 390px, no clipped text, no horizontal page scroll, every tab hits 44px tap target, empty states for the new For Rent tab.

## Files to touch (exact list — do not expand scope)
1. `src/components/ValuationStrip.tsx`
2. `src/components/WhatWeOffer.tsx`
3. `src/components/FeaturedPropertiesClient.tsx`
4. `src/components/OffPlanSectionClient.tsx`
5. `src/components/CommunitiesSection.tsx`
6. `src/components/StatsSection.tsx` (audit only — see item 6)

## Item 1 — ValuationStrip: single compact horizontal row on mobile
- Current mobile layout is stacked (icon + text on top, button below) and visually too tall; user reports it appears clipped.
- Target: single row at ~60px tall on mobile. Layout: `[icon] [headline + subtitle stacked tight] [CTA button]` all on one horizontal line.
- Desktop layout stays unchanged. Use `sm:` breakpoint to switch — mobile = compact row, `sm:` and up = current treatment.
- Headline can truncate with `line-clamp-1`; subtitle `line-clamp-1 text-xs`.
- CTA on mobile becomes a small pill button (compact `px-3 py-2` style from §2 button patterns), still hits 44px min tap by adding `min-h-[44px]`.
- Acceptance: at 390px viewport, the strip is one row, no clipping, tap target ≥44px, content readable, no overflow scroll.
- Edge: headline overflow → truncate, do not wrap. Failure: if CTA is too narrow for label, shorten label on mobile (e.g. 'Get Value' instead of 'Get Free Valuation').

## Item 2 — WhatWeOffer: 2-column icon-card grid on mobile
- Current mobile: horizontal scroll of 62%-wide cards with 130px image headers. Image-heavy, requires scroll to see all services.
- Replace mobile layout with a **2-column grid** of compact icon-only cards. NO images on mobile. 4–6 cards fit in viewport without scrolling.
- Each mobile card: small lucide icon (h-5 w-5 or h-6 w-6) in a tinted square (accent gold or primary green tint, your judgment per DESIGN_SYSTEM glass/tint patterns), title (text-sm font-semibold), 1-line description (text-xs text-muted-foreground line-clamp-1 or line-clamp-2).
- Desktop layout stays exactly as it is. Use Tailwind responsive classes — mobile grid, `md:` switches to current desktop treatment.
- Card style must match existing site card vocabulary: `bg-card border border-border/50 rounded-xl p-4` (or similar from §2 cards). No new card style.
- Pick the icon for each service from `lucide-react` (already in deps) — use semantically obvious icons (e.g. Home, Building2, Key, TrendingUp, etc.). DEV picks the mapping.
- Acceptance: at 390px, all service cards visible in a single 2-column grid, no horizontal scroll, no images on mobile, tap targets ≥44px (whole card is the tap target).

## Item 3 — FeaturedPropertiesClient: Secondary Market with For Sale / For Rent tabs
- Rename the section eyebrow/heading copy to position this as 'Secondary Market' listings (resale/rentals, distinct from off-plan). Heading: 'Secondary Market'. Eyebrow keeps the existing gold uppercase style (see DESIGN_SYSTEM section label pattern).
- Add a 2-tab segmented control above the grid: **For Sale** / **For Rent**. Active tab uses brand green (`bg-[#0B3D2E] text-white`), inactive uses neutral (`bg-background text-muted-foreground`). Pill or underline style — match what's already used elsewhere on the site (check `ProjectDetailClient.tsx` tab style as reference).
- **Field check (DEV must verify before coding the filter):** open the listings response shape. Likely fields: `transactionType`, `status`, `listingType`, or `category`. Grep `src/components/FeaturedProperties*.tsx` and `src/types/` to confirm. If a field exists distinguishing sale vs rent, filter client-side by it. If NO such field exists, fall back: 'For Sale' shows all current listings (the existing default), 'For Rent' shows an empty state with a 'Browse rentals →' CTA linking to `/rent`.
- Empty state for For Rent (when no rentals or no field): a centered card with friendly copy ('Looking for a rental? Browse our full rentals catalog →') linking to `/rent`. Copy voice per DESIGN_SYSTEM (warm, specific, second-person).
- Spacing tightening (mobile): `py-12 sm:py-24` → `py-8 sm:py-20`. Heading block: `mb-6 sm:mb-14` → `mb-4 sm:mb-10`.
- Tabs must be ≥44px tap height. Tab state lives in component-level `useState`. Default tab: 'For Sale'.
- Acceptance: section renamed; tabs render; switching tabs swaps grid (or shows empty state); mobile spacing reduced; no flicker on initial render.
- Edge: if the underlying listings endpoint already only returns sale listings, that's fine — For Rent shows the empty-state CTA. Document this in devReport.

## Item 4 — OffPlanSectionClient: spacing only
- `py-14 sm:py-24` → `py-10 sm:py-20`
- Heading margin: `mb-8 sm:mb-14` → `mb-5 sm:mb-10`
- Do NOT touch anything else in this component. Horizontal scroll, card layout, copy all stay identical.

## Item 5 — CommunitiesSection: visual upgrade on mobile
- Add a proper eyebrow label above the section title: gold uppercase, matching the section label pattern in DESIGN_SYSTEM (`text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.3em] text-accent font-semibold`). Copy: 'Communities' or 'Explore Dubai' (DEV picks the one that reads best alongside the existing heading; check what the existing heading says first to avoid duplication).
- Mobile card width: `w-[60%]` → `w-[72%]` (better readability, fewer cards visible but each is legible).
- Mobile card aspect ratio: `aspect-[3/4]` → `aspect-[4/3]` (landscape since the card is wider now). Desktop ratio stays untouched if different.
- Stronger bottom gradient overlay so the title text reads cleanly. Use existing pattern: gradient from `from-black/80 via-black/40 to-transparent` (or stronger) bottom-up. Title stays white.
- Add an 'Explore →' affordance on each card — small pill or text label bottom-right or bottom-left, white text with subtle backdrop (use the green glass pattern from DESIGN_SYSTEM: `backdrop-blur-sm bg-white/10 border border-white/20`). Should look interactive but not heavy.
- Section padding: `py-12 sm:py-24` → `py-8 sm:py-20`.
- Acceptance: eyebrow visible above heading, mobile cards landscape at 72% width, gradient strong enough to read titles on any image, Explore affordance present and styled.
- Edge: if cards already have a CTA or chevron, replace it with the Explore label rather than stacking both.

## Item 6 — General padding audit
- Already handled: FeaturedPropertiesClient (item 3), OffPlanSectionClient (item 4), CommunitiesSection (item 5).
- **Audit StatsSection.tsx** (`src/components/StatsSection.tsx`): if it uses `py-16 sm:py-24` or larger, reduce mobile to `py-10 sm:py-20`. Do NOT change desktop. If existing mobile is already ≤`py-10`, leave it alone and note in devReport.
- Do NOT touch any other section. Scope is bounded.

## Interaction matrix
- Item 3 (For Sale / For Rent tabs) × existing listings hydration in `FeaturedPropertiesServer.tsx` parent → check: the server passes a fixed prop set; client-side filter must work on whatever shape is already passed in, do not introduce a new fetch.
- Item 1 (ValuationStrip compact) × existing valuation flow CTA targets → check: the CTA href stays the same, only the visual shrinks.
- Item 2 (WhatWeOffer grid) × no shared state, safe.
- Item 5 (CommunitiesSection cards) × existing community link routes → check: clicking the card still navigates to the same `/communities/[slug]` route the existing card uses; do not break the link.

## demoPath (user click-through)
1. Open `http://localhost:3000` on a 390px mobile viewport.
2. See compact ValuationStrip at top (one row, ~60px tall).
3. Scroll: see WhatWeOffer as a 2-column grid of icon cards, no images, no horizontal scroll.
4. Scroll: see 'Secondary Market' heading with 'For Sale' / 'For Rent' tabs. Switch to 'For Rent' → see either filtered rentals or empty-state CTA.
5. Scroll: see Off-Plan section, tighter spacing.
6. Scroll: see Communities with gold eyebrow label, wider landscape cards, strong gradient, 'Explore →' affordance on each card.
7. Confirm no horizontal page scroll, no clipped content, all tap targets feel reachable.

## Design constraints (apply to all items)
- DESIGN_SYSTEM.md is authoritative — reuse existing button, card, glass, gradient patterns. No new tokens.
- Brand green gradient (exact): `linear-gradient(135deg, #0B3D2E, #1A7A5A)` — copy verbatim if used.
- Gold accent eyebrows: `text-xs uppercase tracking-[0.3em] text-accent font-semibold`.
- Mobile tap targets ≥44px.
- No `text-foreground` on dark/colored bg — use `text-white*`.
- No new floating fixed elements.
- All existing desktop layouts must remain visually unchanged — every change is mobile-first using `sm:` / `md:` breakpoints to preserve current desktop treatment.

## Acceptance (run after coding)
- `npx tsc --noEmit` passes.
- Visit `/` at 390px width: all six checkpoints from demoPath verified.
- Visit `/` at 1280px width: zero visible regression — every section looks identical to before.
- No new lucide imports beyond what's needed for item 2 icons.

1. ValuationStrip — single compact row on mobile, ~60px tall, [icon][title+subtitle][CTA].

findings.issue: Icon has both className='h-5 w-5 text-white' and style={{ color: '#D4A847' }} — the inline style always wins, making className color redundant. Harmless but inconsistent.

findings.suggestedFix: Either add a translation key or note this as intentionally en-only in a comment.

reviewerReport.summary: Pure UI change across 5 components. No auth, no API routes, no shared state touched. TypeScript passes cleanly. All spec items delivered: compact mobile ValuationStrip with min-h-[44px] CTA, WhatWeOffer 2-col icon grid (desktop images intact), FeaturedPropertiesClient renamed with working tabs + empty state, OffPlanSectionClient spacing-only, CommunitiesSection eyebrow + wider landscape cards + Explore affordance. Brand green gradient used verbatim where present. next/link vs @/navigation is pre-existing in all 3 files, not introduced by this diff. 3 minor i18n/style nits, none blocking.

No vertical stacking, no clipping.

summary: Global CurrencyContext with live rates wired to Navbar, ProjectDetailClient, PropertyDetailClient, SearchPageClient, OffPlanPageClient, ListingsPageClient
contextGaps: ProjectDetailClient's local CURRENCY_RATES/CURRENCY_SYMBOLS/formatPrice block was ~35 lines at module scope (lines 57–91 in original). Removing it and aliasing useCurrency() format/rates inside the component required updating 15+ formatPrice() call sites throughout the ~2700-line file — the secondary ~USD display lines were spread widely including hero, stat cards, payment plan milestones, CTA sidebar, and mobile CTA.
PropertyDetailClient had 4 USD_RATE usage sites: hero, stats strip, mobile CTA, sidebar CTA. All cleanly removable by replacing formattedPrice derivation with fmtPrice().

The ListingsPageClient local formatPrice() was a per-listing function (took a Listing object, not a price number). Replacing it with fmtCurrency() required switching the call site to pass l.price directly. The function was then dead code and removed to avoid noUnusedLocals TS errors.

SearchPageClient's formatProjectPrice import came from @/lib/formatPrice — simply swapping the import for useCurrency and using fmtCurrency() was sufficient. The module-level formatPrice function (line 99) was left as-is since module-level unused functions don't trigger TS errors.
/api/currency-rates correctly returns {} (empty object) when serverApiUrl returns a relative path (i.e. API_BASE_URL not set in dev). CurrencyProvider falls back to FALLBACK_RATES in that case.
CurrencyProvider is outermost — wraps SessionProvider — so useCurrency() is available even inside next-auth callbacks if needed.
